subtitle: The Farmer Who Dreamed in Colours

panels.shot: epic mid-shot, slight low angle, flag design spread before him, stormy sky behind
panels.action: Pingali Venkayya stands in a rustic courtyard, aged yet unbowed, one hand on a rough sketch of a tricolour flag on the ground, as a distant swirl of countless unseen flags rises into a cloudy Indian sky.

dialogue.text: Before India had a flag to salute, a quiet farmer–scholar from Andhra spent a lifetime chasing three colours and a spinning wheel. How did his dream become the nation’s symbol, yet his name fade?

i18n.hi: भारत के पास सलामी देने लायक अपना झंडा नहीं था, पर आंध्र का एक शांत किसान–विद्वान उम्र भर तीन रंगों और चरखे का पीछा करता रहा। उसका सपना राष्ट्र का चिन्ह बना, पर नाम क्यों ओझल हो गया?

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of coastal Andhra village at dawn
panels.action: A young Pingali Venkayya walks barefoot along the fields near Bhatlapenumarru, early sun over the Krishna delta, palm trees and wet earth framing his small figure.

dialogue.text: In the 1870s, in the wet green fields of Bhatlapenumarru in coastal Andhra, a boy named Pingali Venkayya grew up between soil and sky, hearing whispers of a rising nation in distant towns.

i18n.hi: १८७० के दशक में, तटीय आंध्र के भीगे हरे खेतों में, भातलपेणुमर्रु के आकाश–मिट्टी के बीच पिंगाली वेंकय्या नाम का लड़का दूर–दूर के कस्बों से उठती आज़ादी की फुसफुसाहट सुनकर बड़ा हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot, classroom interior, low-angle focus on attentive face
panels.action: Teenaged Venkayya sits in a simple classroom, maps and charts on the walls, his eyes fixed intently on a teacher pointing at a globe.

dialogue.text: He was a farmer’s son, yet his mind wandered far. Geology, languages, the flags of distant empires—each strip of cloth on the globe told him how power announced itself to the world.

i18n.hi: वह किसान का बेटा था, पर दिमाग दूर-दूर भटकता था। भू-विज्ञान, भाषाएँ, दूर के साम्राज्यों के झंडे—दुनिया के हर टुकड़े कपड़े से उसे दिखता कि ताकत खुद को दुनिया के सामने कैसे दिखाती है।

panels.shot: dynamic montage-like wide shot, slight bird’s-eye, showing him traveling
panels.action: A composite scene shows young Venkayya on a train platform, then at a mine site examining rocks, then listening to a nationalist speech in a crowded town square.

dialogue.text: As he travelled for work and study—a farmer, a geologist, a restless patriot—he saw the Union Jack fly above every station and office. India, he noticed, marched under flags that were never hers.

i18n.hi: काम और पढ़ाई के सफ़र में—किसान, भूवैज्ञानिक, बेचैन देशभक्त—हर स्टेशन, हर दफ्तर पर उसे यूनियन जैक ही लहराता दिखा। उसने देखा, भारत उन झंडों के नीचे चलता है जो उसके अपने नहीं हैं।

panels.shot: intimate close-up on his hands sketching, top-down desk view
panels.action: By lamplight in a modest room, Venkayya bends over a rough wooden table, sketching lines and bands on paper, small swatches of coloured cloth scattered around.

dialogue.text: In the quiet hours he began to draw. Lines, bands, colours. Could a flag hold a land of many tongues, faiths and castes? Could a simple cloth become a rallying cry, yet offend no one?

i18n.hi: खामोश घंटों में वह बनाने लगा—रेखाएँ, पट्टियाँ, रंग। क्या एक झंडा इतनी भाषाओं, मजहबों, जातियों वाले देश को समेट सकता है? क्या साधारण कपड़ा बिगाड़े बिना सबको एक नारे में बाँध सकता है?

panels.shot: medium shot, pamphlet foregrounded in his hands
panels.action: Venkayya, now older, sits upright, proudly holding freshly printed Telugu pamphlets, as a small village press clanks in the background.

dialogue.text: By 1916 he turned thought into print. In his Telugu pamphlet, Bharata Desabhimani, he argued that a national movement needed a national flag—clear, shared, carried by all who sought swaraj.

i18n.hi: १९१६ तक उसने सोच को छपाई में बदल दिया। अपने तेलुगु पैम्फलेट ‘भारत देशाभिमानी’ में उसने लिखा कि राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन को एक राष्ट्रीय झंडा चाहिए—साफ, साझा, जिसे हर स्वराज चाहने वाला उठा सके।

panels.shot: wide shot of a small meeting, community hall, slight low angle
panels.action: In a modest hall, Venkayya addresses a handful of nationalist workers, holding up a hand-sewn tricolour prototype, faces in the crowd curious and uncertain.

dialogue.speaker: pingali_venkayya
dialogue.text: A flag will bind our marches from Madras to Lahore.

i18n.hi: एक झंडा हमारी रैलियों को मद्रास से लाहौर तक बाँध देगा।

panels.shot: wide crowd shot at a Congress gathering, dust and banners in air
panels.action: A bustling Indian National Congress gathering in Vijayawada around 1921; tents, crowds and banners, with Venkayya weaving through, clutching a carefully folded flag.

dialogue.text: By the early 1920s his experiments multiplied. At Congress gatherings he arrived with flag after flag, testing colours and symbols, urging leaders to see what he had glimpsed in his mind.

i18n.hi: २० के दशक की शुरुआत तक उसके प्रयोग बढ़ते गए। कांग्रेस की सभाओं में वह एक के बाद एक झंडा लेकर आता, रंग और निशानियाँ आज़माता, नेताओं से वह दृश्य मांगता जो उसे मन की आँखों में दिखा था।

panels.shot: mid-shot two-figure composition from behind Venkayya’s shoulder (Gandhi off-screen implied, not shown)
panels.action: In a shaded pandal at the 1921 Vijayawada Congress, Venkayya respectfully presents his tricolour design to a simply dressed elder figure seated before him, the elder’s hand gesturing thoughtfully toward the cloth.

dialogue.text: At Vijayawada in 1921 he laid one such tricolour before Mahatma Gandhi. The design would not stay frozen; in that dialogue between a designer and a leader, new colours were about to enter.

i18n.hi: १९२१, विजयवाड़ा में उसने ऐसा ही एक तिरंगा महात्मा गांधी के सामने रख दिया। डिज़ाइन यहीं थमने वाला नहीं था; डिज़ाइनर और नेता की उस बातचीत में अब नए रंग दाख़िल होने वाले थे।

panels.shot: close-up of flag laid on mat, top-down, hands gesturing over it
panels.action: On a woven mat lies Venkayya’s tricolour design; two hands, one his, the other belonging to a simply robed elder, hover over the cloth as if rearranging its meaning.

dialogue.text: The record remembers Gandhi suggesting a white band and the spinning wheel—symbols of peace and khadi—into the tricolour tradition Venkayya had brought. From then, Congress flags would carry this evolving pattern.

i18n.hi: रिकॉर्ड बताते हैं कि गांधी ने सफेद पट्टी और चरखे का सुझाव दिया—शांति और खादी के चिन्ह—उन्हें वेंकय्या के बनाए तिरंगे में जोड़कर। इसके बाद कांग्रेस के झंडों पर यही बदलती हुई बनावट दिखने लगी।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of protest march, flags high, slightly low angle
panels.action: A 1920s protest march moves through an Indian town; young men and women hold aloft tricolour flags with the charkha at centre, while Venkayya watches from a doorway, eyes reflective.

dialogue.text: Across the 1920s and 1930s, these Congress flags—tricolour with the charkha—appeared in marches and satyagrahas. They were not yet the state’s flag, but for millions they meant defiance and hope.

i18n.hi: १९२०–३० के दशक में यही कांग्रेस के झंडे—चरखे वाला तिरंगा—रैलियों और सत्याग्रहों में लहराए। वे अभी राज का झंडा नहीं थे, पर लाखों के लिए वे चुनौती और उम्मीद बन चुके थे।

panels.shot: medium shot, indoor committee room, papers on table
panels.action: A formal committee room scene from 1931 is suggested: leaders seated around a table strewn with flag sketches, while outside the window a tricolour flutters faintly.

dialogue.text: In 1931, within the Indian National Congress, a Flag Committee examined designs and colours. Their report spoke of a tricolour with the charkha at its heart—a pattern now rooted in years of experimentation.

i18n.hi: १९३१ में, इंडियन नेशनल कांग्रेस के भीतर ‘फ्लैग कमिटी’ ने रंगों और नमूनों की जाँच की। उनकी रिपोर्ट में बीच में चरखे वाला तिरंगा था—एक बनावट जो वर्षों के प्रयोग से जड़ पकड़ चुकी थी।

panels.shot: introspective close-up on an older Venkayya reading a paper
panels.action: An ageing Venkayya sits in a modest veranda, spectacles low on his nose, reading a newspaper report about the Congress flag, the distant sound of a procession carrying flags in the background.

dialogue.speaker: pingali_venkayya
dialogue.text: The flag now walks farther than I ever could.

i18n.hi: अब मेरा झंडा वहाँ तक चल चुका है जहाँ मैं कभी नहीं पहुँच सकता था।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of the Constituent Assembly hall interior, slightly elevated
panels.action: Inside the Constituent Assembly Hall in New Delhi on 22 July 1947, members sit facing the Speaker’s chair, the atmosphere charged, as a large rolled-up flag rests on a stand at the side.

dialogue.text: Then came 22 July 1947. In the Constituent Assembly, leaders debated and adopted the flag of independent India—a tricolour whose central charkha was replaced by the Ashoka Chakra from the Sarnath lion capital.

i18n.hi: फिर आया २२ जुलाई १९४७। संविधान सभा में नेताओं ने बहस कर आज़ाद भारत का झंडा अपनाया—तिरंगा जिसमें बीच का चरखा सारनाथ के सिंह स्तंभ से लिया अशोक चक्र से बदला गया।

panels.shot: close-up of hands unfurling the new tricolour, mid-level angle
panels.action: Hands of Assembly members unfurl the new tricolour indoors, saffron, white and green spreading out, with the navy-blue Ashoka Chakra emerging in the centre.

dialogue.text: The Constituent Assembly debates record the choice clearly: the wheel of law, the Ashoka Chakra, would speak of motion and dharma. The charkha receded; the tricolour tradition remained, now made the Republic’s emblem.

i18n.hi: संविधान सभा की बहस साफ दर्ज करती है: धर्मचक्र, अशोक चक्र, गति और धर्म का संदेश देगा। चरखा पीछे हट गया; तिरंगे की परंपरा बची रही, अब गणराज्य का आधिकारिक चिन्ह बनकर।

panels.shot: medium shot of Venkayya in his later years, rural home interior
panels.action: In the early 1950s, an elderly Venkayya sits on a simple cot in a bare room, a folded tricolour resting beside him, as he quietly writes, the light soft and fading.

dialogue.text: Scholars of flags now trace this arc carefully. They note how many minds shaped the final design, and yet how central Venkayya’s early tricolour experiments were in giving the movement a visual language.

i18n.hi: झंडे के विद्वान आज इस सफ़र को बारीकी से जोड़ते हैं। वे दिखाते हैं कि कितने दिमाग अंतिम डिज़ाइन में जुड़े, फिर भी शुरुआती तिरंगे के प्रयोगों से आंदोलन की दृश्य भाषा गढ़ने में वेंकय्या कितने अहम थे।

panels.shot: somber wide shot of a small funeral procession, distant, rural setting
panels.action: A small group of villagers carries a simple bier down a dusty path in 1963; in a corner of the frame, an unfurled Indian flag flies over a public building, unnoticed by the mourners.

dialogue.text: In 1963, the man from Bhatlapenumarru died with little ceremony and fewer honours. The flag he helped midwife was by then everywhere—in schools, offices, barracks—yet his name seldom travelled with it.

i18n.hi: १९६३ में भातलपेणुमर्रु का यह आदमी बिना शोर–शराबे, बिना बड़े सम्मान के चल बसा। जिस झंडे को उसने जन्म देने में मदद की, वह तब तक स्कूलों, दफ्तरों, छावनियों पर था—पर उसका नाम शायद ही साथ उड़ता था।

panels.shot: poetic close-up profile of Venkayya’s statue or imagined bust, flag blurred behind
panels.action: A sculpted likeness of Pingali Venkayya stands in soft light, his gaze lifted, while behind him, slightly out of focus, the Indian tricolour ripples against a clear sky.

dialogue.text: Recent historians in Andhra and beyond have begun to stitch his story back into the cloth of the flag—placing his work among the many hands that turned a protest banner into a state’s symbol.

i18n.hi: आंध्र और बाहर के नए इतिहासकार उसकी कहानी फिर से झंडे के कपड़े में पिरो रहे हैं—उसके काम को उन कई हाथों के बीच जगह देते हुए जिन्होंने विरोध के बैनर को राज्य के प्रतीक में बदला।

panels.shot: final wide shot, low angle, multiple flags on horizon, Venkayya’s silhouette in foreground
panels.action: Silhouetted against a vast twilight sky dotted with soaring tricolours, the figure of Pingali Venkayya stands at the edge of a field, one hand outstretched toward the fluttering banners on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Each time the tricolour rises today, it carries not just a state’s authority but a century of ideas, debates and quiet labour—and among those early threads runs the patient hand of Pingali Venkayya, farmer of flags.

i18n.hi: आज जब भी तिरंगा उठता है, वह सिर्फ राज्य की सत्ता नहीं, एक सदी के विचारों, बहसों और शांत मेहनत को लेकर ऊँचा होता है—और उन शुरुआती धागों के बीच कहीं पिंगाली वेंकय्या का धैर्यवान हाथ भी है, झंडों का किसान।

subtitle_i18n.en: The Farmer Who Dreamed in Colours
subtitle_i18n.hi: रंगों में सपने देखने वाला किसान
